component.name: USB Diagnostics
component.summary: See what a USB-C cable, port, and charger actually negotiated

description.p: A native viewer for the state Linux already knows about your USB-C ports, cables, chargers, and devices — and for the conclusions that state supports. It reads sysfs and the kernel log, needs no privileges, and updates live as things are plugged and unplugged.

Each port and device gets a one-sentence verdict, the checks that were ruled out, the findings that fired, and a bottleneck chain showing where power or speed stops. Every finding carries how much to trust it — measured, inferred, or a heuristic — and where a question cannot be answered on this hardware, the app says so instead of leaving a gap.
It cannot measure a cable electrically. Signal integrity, CC-line voltages, and the true rating of an unmarked cable are invisible to software and need a hardware analyzer.

First release of the graphical viewer: port and device tree, verdicts, exonerations, findings, and the power and data bottleneck chains, updating live from udev. Read-only; the privileged probes stay in the command-line tool behind an explicit consent gate.
